copy.blurb:
This is a Pick. Belgium v IR Iran in FIFA World Cup 2026 on Sunday, and the model and the market disagree on the IR Iran side by +14.8pp. That's the gap the verdict rests on.

The Elo prior reads Belgium 1860 vs IR Iran 1740: 120 points in favour of Belgium, which is a meaningful but not decisive prior. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Belgium to win at 51%, the draw at 23%, and IR Iran to win at 26%. The Desk's three-way distribution is calibrated against the W/D/L resolution Polymarket and Kalshi settle on, not against the exact scoreline. IR Iran sits at 26% of the mass.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Belgium to win at 67%, the draw at 20%, and IR Iran to win at 11%. Polymarket has IR Iran at 11%, which prices out at American odds of +809; the model has the same side at 26%. The +14.8pp gap across them is the disagreement we're surfacing.

The +3pp Pick threshold isn't on the point estimate, it's on the 5th-percentile from a 100-sample bootstrap of the Elo prior plus bonuses. On IR Iran, that haircut lands the model at 21%; the market is at 11%. Even on the conservative reading, the gap is +10.0pp. We're not arguing the market is broadly wrong; the closing line and the model are in approximate agreement across recent fixtures by Brier score. The claim is narrower: this side specifically reads mispriced.

News will move the prior. With kickoff 30 days out, we're still on weekly refresh; the daily cadence picks up inside T-5d. On a Pick this wide, it would take material news — a missing star, a tournament dropout, a venue change — to collapse the gap below the +3pp threshold; on the narrower side of the field, a single refresh can flip Pick to Pass. Either way, the Desk re-publishes after each refresh and does not recommend a trade.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives IR Iran a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +14.8pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: A +14.8pp gap across model and market on the IR Iran side. Our Elo prior, after host and altitude adjustments, rates IR Iran at 26%; Polymarket sits at 11%.
copy.title: Belgium v IR Iran · the model leans IR Iran
